maria: Quick q — replay harness shows TTFT p95 jumps ~2x when we switch kernel selection strategy, but QPS and goodput look almost identical. How do folks normalize comparisons so we don't chase noise?
kevin: first, make sure kernel is pinned. if kernel-selection runs at request time you get scheduling variance. pin kernels and reuse same model binary.
sam: short plan i've used: 1) pin kernel, 2) run a warmup phase for KV cache, 3) fix batching policy, 4) run both synthetic and replay with same input length distribution.
jena: nv — also disable autoscaler / burst pools so capacity is constant. small capacity changes create tail latency variance.
maria: ok — how are we defining TTFT/TPOT precisely for these runs? slight differences in defs break comparisons.
kevin: our defs: TTFT = time from request accepted by frontend to first token byte emitted by runtime (includes scheduling + kernel launch). TPOT = median per-token production time once streaming begins (tokens / token-time). record p50/p95/p99 for both.
sam: add: measure "cold" vs "warm" TTFT. cold = after model load or after KV miss path; warm = with KV hit and cache warmed. report both separately.
jena: goodput vs QPS: goodput = total user-visible tokens / wall-clock time (accounts for partial and batched outputs). QPS = requests per second. show both because batching can lower QPS but increase goodput.
maria: examples/helpful commands?
sam: example replay command we use:
```
./harness/replay --trace traces/nov-replay.json --pin-kernel=mkldnn --kv-warmup=500 --ramp=180 --duration=600
```
jena: also capture perf counters + kernel selection logs:
```
journalctl -u runtime -f | grep "kernel="
perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -o perf.out ./bin/runtime-test
```
kevin: important to normalize "effective tokens" across workloads. weight your synthetic inputs to match production token-length histogram. otherwise TPOT comparisons are meaningless.
maria: sample log line format we should standardize on?
sam: something compact we parse: `[INFO] TTFT_p95=72ms TTFT_p99=210ms TPOT=1.8ms_per_token goodput=12.5k_tok/s QPS=230 kernel=nvfuser kv_hit_rate=0.87`
jena: +1 to including kv_hit_rate and avg_batch_size. those explain differences fast.
kevin: for apples-to-apples between synthetic and replay: run both with identical prefix distributions and same KV-warmup behavior. if replay has many repeated prefixes, consider deduping to avoid inflated cache hit rates.
maria: action items: @sam will run A/B with pinned kernels + standardized log output, @jena add kv-warmup flag to replay harness and include kv_hit_rate in logs, @kevin will share a short doc with exact TTFT/TPOT/Goodput formulas. i'll collate results and post summary. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will watch the job and follow up with a small dashboard for p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT comparisons.
